title: 2.0: Mapping generics with typing.Annotated does not work if "from __future__ import annotations" is included

labels.name: orm - annotated declarative
labels.description: issues with the new annotations-based declarative ORM approach

milestone.title: 2.0 final
milestone.description: can be looked at during the beta release period for 2.0.

body:
### Describe the bug

When `from __future__ import annotation` is included, then it's not possible to map generic collections to SQL types.
Mapping process throws the exception. If we change `list[X]` to `list`, then it works, but won't be fully correct from typing point of view.
My use case is I'm trying to map `list[str]` or `Sequence[str]` or `Sequence[SomeEnum]` to `JSONB` field in PostgreSQL, resulting in JSON array stored in this field.

### To Reproduce

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Annotated
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, registry, Mapped, mapped_column
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB
from uuid import UUID

TestType = Annotated[list[str], 0]

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    registry = registry(
        type_annotation_map={
            TestType: JSONB()
        }
    )

class Test(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'test'

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    data: Mapped[TestType] = mapped_column()
```
